blocks.text: Falcon Perfumes is a perfume retail website that helps customers explore fragrances, inspect product photos and notes, and place cash-on-delivery orders. The target audience is fragrance shoppers looking for a clear product catalogue and store staff who need a simple way to maintain stock and orders.

The starting point was four supplied HTML pages: Home, New Arrivals, Brands and Contact. The submission converts their page roles into shared PHP templates, recreates missing CSS and JavaScript assets, and retains the navy-and-gold visual identity. Generic stock photos were replaced by product-matched images.

blocks.text: The application has no external CSS/JavaScript CDN dependency and uses bundled images. It runs locally without an internet connection after XAMPP and the database are set up.

All application tables use InnoDB and utf8mb4. Foreign keys maintain relationships; DECIMAL fields store monetary values. Product and customer records are retained where historic orders depend on them.

blocks.text: How a request is processed

A PHP page loads the shared functions and PDO configuration. Protected routes validate the relevant customer or admin session. On POST, the handler checks the CSRF token and validates all submitted values before using a prepared SQL statement. Successful writes redirect to a fresh GET request, which displays a confirmation message and current database values.

The product page is reached by selecting a product card image or name. Its ID selects the database record and gallery; invalid or archived products return HTTP 404. There is no separate Product Page item in the navigation.

Registration accepts a username, email and password with confirmation. PHP checks input length, username format, email validity, uniqueness and password matching. Passwords use password_hash(..., PASSWORD_BCRYPT); login uses password_verify(). Password input is limited to 10-72 bytes to avoid bcrypt truncation.

blocks.caption: Figure 1. Registration page rendered by the PHP application.

blocks.text: After valid login, session_regenerate_id(true) replaces the session ID before the customer reaches dashboard.php. Logout accepts a CSRF-protected POST and destroys the session and cookie. Five failed sign-ins for the same identity/IP within 15 minutes temporarily block further attempts.

The customer dashboard queries only orders belonging to the current account. Disabling a customer in the admin panel prevents future login and removes protected-page access on the next request. Admins use a separate table, session name and cookie path; customer registration cannot grant staff privileges.

blocks.text: The collection supports search suggestions, collapsible filters, price sorting and pagination. Related products below each detail page come from the same brand. Prices are editable demonstration values inherited from the frontend, not current market quotations.

blocks.caption: Figure 3. Protected product management list, with prices, stock and availability controls.

blocks.text: Every protected admin page loads the staff-session guard before rendering. The temporary admin password must be changed at first login. Staff can add or edit perfumes, manage brands and categories, upload multiple photos, choose the cover image, remove gallery images and archive or restore a product.

Uploads accept JPEG, PNG and WebP after MIME and image-dimension checks. Each photo is limited to 5 MB and 20 megapixels, and a product must retain 2-8 images. Uploaded filenames are random; executable extensions are blocked in the upload directory.

The In Stock / Sold Out control updates a database flag. Zero stock also makes a product unavailable. The storefront shows a red SOLD OUT badge and a disabled grey purchase button. PHP repeats availability checks for cart updates and order placement, so editing browser HTML cannot purchase an unavailable product.
Low-stock warnings appear at five units or fewer. A brand or category linked to a product cannot be deleted until its references are removed or reassigned.

pages.title: 07 / Implementation
pages.subtitle: Orders, stock transactions and dashboard totals

blocks.caption: Figure 4. Admin overview with demonstration order totals and low-stock warnings.

blocks.text: The cart stores product IDs and quantities in the customer session. Prices and totals are loaded from the database. Checkout requires login and a delivery name, phone and address. The server calculates totals in integer cents, applies USD 5 delivery below USD 50, and creates a cash-on-delivery order.

Order creation runs inside an InnoDB transaction. Product rows are locked in a consistent ID order, stock is rechecked and decremented, and the order plus items are saved together. A unique checkout token and redirect prevent accidental duplicate submissions.

Cancellation restores each quantity once, under an order-row lock. The dashboard counts total orders, customers, unread messages and delivered revenue. Revenue includes shipping on Delivered cash-on-delivery orders; no online payment settlement is claimed.

blocks.caption: Figure 5. Contact form connected to the messages table.

blocks.text: The contact form collects name, email and message. Client-side and server-side checks enforce valid lengths and email format. A valid CSRF-protected request inserts a prepared statement into messages, then redirects with a success confirmation. A short session-based cooldown limits repeated submissions.

The admin Messages page lists sender details, timestamp and query, with read/unread controls. Message text is escaped before rendering; a test containing script markup appeared as text and did not execute. This implementation stores enquiries but does not send emails.

The Customers page shows registered users and their order histories. Staff can disable and re-enable accounts. Public contact details from the original mockup were not treated as verified business information, so the finished contact page focuses on the working enquiry form and order assistance.

blocks.text: Completed verification

Real HTTP and browser tests exercised customer registration and duplicate rejection, login session rotation, admin isolation, missing-CSRF rejection, SQL-injection login rejection, escaped stored text, cart pricing, order creation, duplicate checkout, stock changes, cancellation, account disabling, product CRUD, image upload validation and taxonomy constraints.

Chromium checks verified gallery switching, mobile menu behavior, loaded product images, no JavaScript errors and no horizontal overflow on six customer pages at 390 px. PHP source files passed syntax checks. Read-only CLI smoke checks validate tables, gallery files and bcrypt hashes. The detailed check list is in tests/TEST-RESULTS.md.

Test environment: PHP 8.3.6, MariaDB 10.11.14 and Chromium 131 on Linux. The XAMPP graphical control panel was not run here; the student group must complete the documented XAMPP run before submission. Screenshots use temporary demonstration accounts and orders, which are excluded from the shipped database.

pages.title: 10 / Setup instructions
pages.subtitle: Run locally in XAMPP and export with phpMyAdmin

blocks.text: Install and import
1. Install XAMPP with PHP 8.2+ and start Apache and MySQL. Extract the ZIP and place the inner falcon-perfumes folder in C:\xampp\htdocs\. On macOS use /Applications/XAMPP/xamppfiles/htdocs/.

2. Open http://localhost/phpmyadmin. Select Import, choose database.sql and run the SQL import. It creates falcon_perfumes with the tables, catalogue and temporary admin hash. Import into a fresh database; the SQL intentionally avoids dropping existing tables.

3. Check includes/config.php. Local defaults: host 127.0.0.1, port 3306, database falcon_perfumes, username root, blank password, base URL /falcon-perfumes. For changes, copy config.local.example.php to config.local.php and edit that file.
Open and demonstrate
4. Visit http://localhost/falcon-perfumes/. Register a customer through auth/register.php, sign in, open a perfume, add it to the bag and place a cash-on-delivery order.

5. Open http://localhost/falcon-perfumes/admin/login.php. Read the randomly generated temporary username/password in ADMIN-LOGIN.txt. Change the password when prompted. Edit a product, inspect orders and review a contact message.

6. For uploads, enable pdo_mysql, mbstring and fileinfo, and make images/uploads writable. For eight-image batches use upload_max_filesize=5M and post_max_size=45M in php.ini, then restart Apache. Do not open PHP pages by double-clicking them.
Export and submit

7. The included database.sql is a clean MariaDB export generated after testing. To meet the assignment wording exactly, export your local database through phpMyAdmin: select falcon_perfumes, choose Export, Quick, SQL, then Export. Put the resulting database.sql in your submission copy.

8. Complete the report metadata and real contribution records, create/update your GitHub repository and submit the source ZIP, report PDF and repository URL on LMS. The brief says Sunday, 7 September 2026, but that date is a Monday; verify the deadline with the lecturer/LMS.
Troubleshooting

If connection fails, confirm MySQL is running, the database is imported and credentials/port match. If assets fail, correct base_url or remove an extra nested folder. If uploads fail, check PHP size limits and folder permissions. README.md includes CLI smoke checks and the local admin password-reset command.

Scope and remaining limitations

This is an academic local-store implementation with cash on delivery. It does not implement online card payments, automatic email delivery, password-reset emails, two-factor authentication, refunds, a tax engine or courier integration. Admin lists are designed for a small project dataset; the public catalogue is paginated.

For public deployment, replace sample values, verify image-use rights, use a dedicated database user and HTTPS, rotate credentials, restrict setup/report/SQL files and add operational backup and monitoring. Image copyrights remain with their owners. No product photo licensing or affiliation is implied.
Editable report

To complete the report, edit docs/REPORT-CONTENT.json and run python docs/build-report.py with ReportLab and Pillow installed. The included screenshots can be replaced with your own local XAMPP screenshots using the same filenames. Review the regenerated PDF before uploading it.

Documentation and product references for the implementation and catalogue. Product pages and image URLs were retrieved on 27 September 2026. Short descriptions are original summaries. Local filename-to-source mappings appear in docs/image-sources.json.
